title: BlackRock's Tokenized Fund in Hong Kong Takes Stablecoins: What It Means

thumbnail.image_prompt: Hong Kong harbor skyline at night with glowing digital light lines over the water, cinematic, no text, no logos

lines.show: BlackRock has launched a tokenized money market fund in Hong Kong that accepts stablecoins.
According to Cointelegraph, it started with about 100 million dollars in assets.
Here's what happened, how it works, and what it means for everyday crypto users.
The fund is called the BlackRock HKD Digital Liquidity Fund.
lines.say: The fund is called the BlackRock H K D Digital Liquidity Fund.

lines.show: A South China Morning Post report said it launched with roughly 100 million dollars.
BlackRock's documents show the fund began operations on November 16.

scenes.title: Two big seed investors
scenes.text: A bank and a payments company.

lines.show: The seed investors are Standard Chartered, the British banking group, and Ant International.
Ant International is a Singapore-based digital payments company spun out of China's Ant Group.
Both also play wider roles in how the fund runs and gets used.
First, what is a money market fund?
This one invests mainly in short-term government-backed securities and high-grade bank deposits.
Tokenized means fund shares are recorded as tokens on a blockchain.
Here's the key change.
Institutions can stay in a stablecoin instead of converting to cash first.
They put that stablecoin straight into the fund.
And they can take money out in the same stablecoin.

scenes.title: The stablecoin: HKDAP
scenes.text: Pegged to the Hong Kong dollar.

lines.show: The stablecoin used is HKDAP, pegged to the Hong Kong dollar.
lines.say: The stablecoin used is H K D A P, pegged to the Hong Kong dollar.

lines.show: It's issued by Anchorpoint Financial, a joint venture of Standard Chartered, HKT and Animoca Brands.
Standard Chartered is also the fund's custodian, administrator, trustee and tokenization agent.
For Ant International, the fund supports round-the-clock cash management across its operations.
The company says it handles over 20 million transactions a day, across 220 markets.

scenes.title: Institutions first
scenes.text: Retail investors use regular Hong Kong dollars.

lines.show: One important detail: the stablecoin route is for institutional investors.
Retail investors in this fund are limited to conventional Hong Kong dollars.
So what should you take from this?
Large asset managers are putting traditional funds on blockchains.
Stablecoins are being used for more than trading, like moving into and out of funds.
And Hong Kong keeps building: HSBC announced a tokenized fund for retail customers on November 19.

scenes.title: Licensed stablecoin issuers
scenes.text: Hong Kong's first two licenses came in April.

lines.show: HSBC and Anchorpoint Financial received Hong Kong's first two stablecoin issuer licenses in April.
That was eight months after the city's stablecoin rules took effect.
